verdict.reason: The tests verify mismatches in declaration, HEAD, baseline, implementation fingerprint, resolution fingerprint, profile, worktree cleanliness, and authority readability, but they do not vary the resolved Cargo target directory, crate, feature set, or expected rustdoc JSON path. Thus they do not verify the anchor’s central requirement that reuse is rejected unless every listed execution-identity component matches.

The tests verify the 120-second timeout constant and RustdocOutputLock's standalone contention/fail-closed behavior, but never verify that capture_current actually acquires that lock around the rustdoc export or that a lock acquisition/operation failure prevents exporter invocation, existing-JSON reuse, lockless fallback, and retry.

The test requires capture_current_with_exporter to succeed using rustdoc JSON written before lock acquisition at a path supplied by an exporter that ignores the resolved target. This asserts acceptance of output that did not pass through the resolved target's shared lock and ownership boundary, contrary to the cited fail-closed promise.

The tests verify the 120-second constant and that RustdocOutputLock itself times out under contention, but they never exercise capture_current while its resolved target lock is unavailable or fails. Therefore they do not verify that capture_current stops fail-closed without invoking a lockless export, reusing existing JSON, or retrying after timeout.

The tests verify descriptor-relative fail-closed behavior and rejection of symlinked target directories, but they do not verify that capture_current rejects non-Unix platforms or otherwise unverifiable target directories as the anchor requires.

The tests verify fail-closed rejection for symlinked workspace/target paths and descriptor-relative lock integrity on Unix, but they never verify that capture_current rejects unsupported non-Unix platforms or a target directory whose trusted root cannot be validated. Therefore the cited Unix-only/trusted-root promise is not fully verified.

The tests verify the 120-second constant and direct RustdocOutputLock contention, but never exercise RustdocCrateAdapter::capture_current under lock-acquisition or lock-operation failure. They therefore do not establish that this trait implementation serializes export under that lock or stops without lockless export, existing-JSON reuse, or retry.

The tests verify the 120-second timeout, same-target lock contention, descriptor-relative fail-closed reads, and symlink rejection, but they never demonstrate that RustdocCrateAdapter/capture_current uses a feature-owned dedicated target directory or that every output-producing path—including normal Cargo rustdoc and alternate exporters—passes through the same lock and ownership boundary.

The tests verify the 120-second constant and that RustdocOutputLock reports a bounded contention timeout, but they never exercise RustdocCratePort::capture_current under lock timeout or lock-operation failure. Consequently they do not verify that the adapter stops without lockless export, existing-JSON reuse, or retry after timeout.

verdict.reason: The tests separately verify input-fingerprint ABA resistance, lock contention, descriptor-pinned reads, and fail-closed output replacement, but never verify that capture_current holds one and the same lock continuously across expected-output-path determination, export, output-path validation, and JSON-byte snapshot reading. That central entry-relevant guarantee remains unverified.

The tests show lock contention, descriptor-pinned output reads, fail-closed handling of some target/output replacement cases, and that the fingerprint function detects A-B-A input replacement. However, none exercises capture_current with an input change between its starting snapshot and result construction and asserts rejection, so the promised start-fingerprint comparison before returning the authoritative snapshot remains unverified.

The tests verify lock and fingerprint primitives in isolation, but never exercise the trait implementation to show that capture_current holds the target-directory lock continuously from export through output verification/read, compares start/end input and resolved fingerprints, and rejects the capture on mutation or an undetectable non-cooperating writer. Thus the entry-relevant integrated fail-closed behavior remains unverified.

verdict.reason: The test explicitly accepts and fingerprints an absolute RUSTC tool located outside the workspace (`expect("absolute tool bytes are identity even when they live outside the workspace")`) and also accepts Cargo-home configuration contents as fingerprint inputs. The anchor instead requires inputs outside the authoritative workspace-bounded set—including toolchain and CARGO_HOME contents—to cause an authoritative-input error and fail closed for export and reuse.

The 65-layer execute test verifies fail-closed evaluation and zero rustdoc exports, but it does not provide an otherwise reusable cached result and therefore does not verify that result reuse is also rejected when the 65th layer is required.

The tests verify the 120-second constant, exclusive contention, and lock-protected reads, but never execute this entry while lock acquisition or a lock operation fails. They therefore do not verify that it stops without lockless export, reuse of existing JSON, or retry.

RustdocOutputLock 単体の 120 秒上限、競合排除、descriptor-relative 読み取り、置換・非通常ファイル・symlink の fail-closed は検証しているが、この entry の実行経路が専用 target directory を確保し、通常の Cargo rustdoc と別 exporter を含む全 writer を同じ lock と所有境界へ必ず通すことは検証していない。
RustdocOutputLock 単体では 120 秒の定数と短縮 timeout 時のエラーを確認しているが、この entry を lock 競合または lock 操作失敗下で実行していないため、評価が停止し、lockless export・既存 JSON 再利用・timeout 後 retry を行わないことは検証されていない。

The tests exercise descriptor-relative locked reads, target-generation replacement, non-regular outputs, and symlinked target paths, but none verifies that this entry rejects non-Unix platforms or a target directory whose trusted-root status cannot be verified. Those fail-closed parts of the cited promise remain unverified.

The tests verify Unix descriptor-relative locking and fail-closed rejection of symlinked target directories, but they never verify that rustdoc export and snapshot reuse are rejected on non-Unix platforms or whenever the required trusted-root lock capability is unavailable.

The tests verify lock contention, descriptor-relative reads, generation-replacement detection, and input-change rejection separately, but none demonstrates that this entry holds one and the same lock continuously across expected-output-path determination, export, output-path confirmation, and the final JSON snapshot read. The central end-to-end no-generation-mixing/ABA guarantee therefore remains unverified.
